newsitem.title: USA: CME Nov lumber ends up $28.50, deferreds limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME Nov lumber ends up $28.50, deferreds limit up.

text.p: CME November lumber futures closed up $28.50 at $477.50 per tbf, the highest price since December 1994, and deferred contracts closed up the $10 limit.
A cutback in shipments of deliverable spruce from Canada fueled the buying. Analysts and traders expect CME January 1997 to trade $15 higher Tuesday, when the daily trading limit is expanded to $15.
Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures Trading, said November futures appear posed to set a record high price in coming weeks.
"You are going to have to take the November futures to a level where the sawmill will want to take the risk to make delivery with a penalty," Cunningham said.
Lumber traders said with cash spruce quoted Monday near $445 per tbf, a quota-violation penalty could put the delivered price near $500.
Cunningham believes November futures could reach $500, which would best the current record high for CME lumber of $493.50 set in March 1993.
"I don't see anything standing in the way of an all time high," he said.
Lumber closed up $28.50 to $10.00, with January up the $10 limit at $404.40.
